newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury's Summers backs faster economic growth.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury's Summers backs faster economic growth.

text.p: A senior U.S. official on Monday called for faster economic growth and said he saw no barrier to a further fall in the unemployment rate.

"We've got to keep the economy growing and get it growing even faster," Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers told public television's Nightly Business Report program. "I don't think there is any barrier on where unemployment can go."
The jobless rate in December stood at 5.3 percent, below what some economists believe constitutes full employment.

While Summers acknowledged that the Clinton administration and the Federal Reserve needed to watch for signs that the low jobless rate was fanning inflation, he argued that more flexible markets could lead to less unemployment.
"There is no inherent limit on what this economy is capable of producing," he said.
Summers said that balancing the federal budget was "key" to achieving faster economic growth.

"We've already brought the budget deficit way down," Summers said. "We've got to finish the job and we've got to keep it down for the long-term by making a start on those large entitlement programs," he added, in a reference to spending on Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security.
He declined to give a specific prediction on interest rates should the budget be balanced.

But, he said, "If we continue to focus on strengthening the fundamentals of our economy and bringing down that budget deficit, I'm sure the effect of those actions will be to lower the path of interest rates."
